{{Short description|German university teacher (born 1967)}}
'''Ralph Bock''' (born October 8, 1967 in [[Wolfen, Germany|Wolfen]]) is a German molecular biologist who researches in plant physiology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Armarego-Marriott |first=Tegan |date=2020 |title=Ralph Bock |journal=The Plant Cell |language=en |volume=32 |issue=1 |pages=4–6 |doi=10.1105/tpc.19.00894 |issn=1040-4651 |pmc=6961626 |pmid=31748332}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
After graduating from the [[University of Halle]] in 1993, Bock moved to the [[University of Freiburg]], where he received his doctorate in 1996. Part of his study was carried out at [[Rutgers University]] in the lab of [[Pal Maliga]]'s. After [[habilitation]], Bock headed a research group in Freiburg and became a professor in 1999. In 2001, Bock accepted a faculty position at the [[University of Münster]] as director and professor at the Institute for Plant Biochemistry and Biotechnology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr Ralph Bock |url=https://www.mpimp-golm.mpg.de/10981/Ralph_Bock |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=www.mpimp-golm.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref>

In 2004, Bock moved to Potsdam as Director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Plant Physiology]]; there he heads the Department of Organelle Biology, Biotechnology and Molecular Ecophysiology. Since 2005 he has also been an honorary professor at the [[University of Potsdam]] and since 2016 at the [[Hubei University]], [[Wuhan]] in China.

== Honors and awards ==
In 2010, Bock became a member of the [[German academy of sciences leopoldina|German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]. In 2021, he became a fellow of the [[Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities|Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mitglieder Ralph Bock |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/ralph-bock/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina |language=de-DE}}</ref>
